target_customer: Couples and close pairs, including long distance relationships, who want to talk more meaningfully; consumers who pay a premium subscription
problem: Partners drift apart and avoid deep conversation. The app sends a daily research informed question and reveals each answer only after both respond.
business_model: Consumer freemium app with premium subscription and a points and giveaway mechanic

founders.name: Kadie Okwudili
founders.background_notes: Press spells the name Khadesha Okwudili. A Spectrum News story says the idea came after she had cardiac arrest at 23 and asked why it took almost dying to have deep conversations.

founders.name: Ron Rogge
prior_employers: University of Rochester (professor of clinical psychology)
founders.background_notes: YC page: couples and family researcher with over 25 years experience and over 75 peer reviewed articles.

technical_complexity.rationale: A mobile app that sends daily questions and reveals paired answers; the hard part is content quality and retention, not engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Research backed question set and viral community give some edge, but daily question apps are easy to copy and several existed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or large incumbent copy found in sources opened.

market_need_then: Spectrum News reports the app was released by February 2020 and went viral on TikTok about a year later with over 100,000 installs overnight, evidence of consumer demand in the pandemic era of long distance relationships.

branding.name_origin: Greek word agape meaning unconditional, selfless love, per the company site
branding.domain_note: Uses getdailyagape.com, a prefixed domain, not agape.com.

identity.voice_and_tone: tagline Unconditional love; the new way to say I love you

branding.brand_signature: The daily question ritual shared by a couple and the TikTok viral moment
branding.community_and_virality: TikTok viral spike of over 100,000 installs in a day per Spectrum News; coverage in Refinery29, university news and science outlets.

brand_strength.rationale: Meaningful name and a viral TikTok moment helped awareness, though accent and pronunciation vary and the .com is not owned.

outcome_analysis: Agapé is active with about 6 people and says over 2 million people have received its questions. It went viral on TikTok around 2021 and published a university co-authored pilot study in 2023. Funding is unclear in public sources, so the strength of its financial story cannot be judged.
notes: Funding unverified, so no rounds recorded: PitchBook lists a 1.5M seed on 2021-07-02 and 2M total, FundedIQ 2.8M with a 1.0M grant in Oct 2022, CB Insights 2.35M with a business plan competition, VCBacked lists YC, Samsung NEXT, Harlem Capital, Launch NY and 43North; none confirmed by a press release or second outlet. Founded year not stated on YC page; app released by Feb 2020 per Spectrum News. Competitors empty: only undated listicles and a rival blog (Paired, Lasting, Evergreen) were found, none dated near 2021. Founder education not found in opened sources. Co-founder Rogge named by YC page. No shutdown found. The 2023 pilot study has no control group per an independent review and authors disclosed a conflict of interest.
